findings.title: time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because the test monkeypatches time.sleep
findings.body: test_basic patches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` at the top of the test, and the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` is called through the same `time` module. The intended wait for the flusher threads to process the drift change therefore never happens. The test then calls `step.join()` right after the second poll, so it can pass or fail depending on thread timing. The wait needs to be done in a way the patch does not affect (e.g. a real wait captured before patching, or polling until the expected message appears with a deadline).

findings.title: join() breaks out of the loop on deadline without terminating the remaining flusher processes
findings.body: In the new join(), when the deadline is reached the loop does `break`, which skips the `process.terminate()` call for every remaining process. Previously a single process was always terminated after the wait. Now any flusher processes not yet joined are left running past join(), still holding Redis and Kafka producer connections, and they keep flushing after the consumer thinks it has shut down. The termination should happen for every process regardless of whether the deadline has passed (or the loop should `continue` instead of `break`).

findings.title: New flusher_processes parameter inserted before produce_to_pipe changes positional argument meaning
findings.body: `flusher_processes` was inserted in the middle of the `__init__` signature, ahead of `produce_to_pipe`. Any existing caller that passes `produce_to_pipe` positionally will now have it bound to `flusher_processes`, which is silently wrong rather than a TypeError. Adding the new parameter at the end, or making it keyword-only, would avoid this.

findings.title: Class docstring says one process per shard, which the implementation does not guarantee
findings.body: The docstring says the flusher 'Creates one process per shard', but `max_processes` caps the number of processes and the consumer CLI defaults `--flusher-processes` to 1, so with default settings all shards share a single process. The docstring should describe the cap and the shard-to-process mapping instead.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key: 'shards' here vs 'shard' everywhere else
findings.body: The wait_produce timer uses the tag key `shards`, while the produce timer, segment_size_bytes timing and the unhealthy counter all use `shard`. Dashboards and alerts filtering on `shard` will miss this metric, and the two naming conventions make queries error-prone.

findings.title: Unrelated hasattr/isinstance guideline added to the flusher PR
findings.body: This documentation change adds a hasattr-vs-isinstance anti-pattern example that has nothing to do with the multiprocessed span flusher. The example also does not explain why hasattr is wrong for union types, so it is unclear as guidance. It should be split into its own change or removed from this PR.
